definition: An API feature that lets a request resume from a previously processed prompt prefix, reducing processing time and cost for prompts with repeated content.
whyItMatters: Cache reads cost **0.1×** base input on most models; 5-minute writes cost 1.25× and 1-hour writes 2×. It pays off when the same large prefix repeats.
example: Cache a long system prompt and tool definitions shared by every request.

definition: A content-block field marking a cache breakpoint: the prompt (tools, system, then messages) up to and including that block becomes the cacheable prefix.
whyItMatters: Exam scenarios test **where** to put the breakpoint: after the large, stable content and before anything that changes per request.
example: Put `cache_control` on the last block of a long system prompt; add `"ttl": "1h"` for the 1-hour lifetime.

definition: Asynchronous processing of large volumes of Messages requests at 50% lower cost. Most finish in under 1 hour; unfinished batches expire at 24 hours.
whyItMatters: Choose it for work that doesn't need an immediate response (bulk evaluations, content moderation, data analysis), never for live chat.
example: Submit thousands of product descriptions as one batch, then poll for results. Results stay available for 29 days.
